Both describe the missing hip bend ('instead of hinging at the hips' vs 'the hips aren't bent'); A's text also has the knee sliding forward, which could differ from B's 'the knees aren't bent', but none of A's listed quotes support that, so the material cannot separate them.

'The stance is too narrow' ('you need a base to twist off of') and 'an overly narrow stance width' ('you're here as far as stance width') are the same narrow stance; they differ only in the consequence named (twisting vs pushing).

Both texts describe a static pause before the swing that removes the dynamic load ('Starting the racket statically ... removes swing momentum' vs 'pausing before trunk rotation starts, which destroys the dynamic forearm stretch'); A's quotes only report the resulting feel ('feels stiff and restricted'), so the material offers no visible feature to separate them.

'Let your chest go first, let the arm lag here, and then let it whip through' and 'if I let this go back, I have to make sure I time this stretch reflex' (vs attaching the arm 'to your chest') describe the same arm lagging behind the chest; they differ only in the cost named (control vs timing).

Both show the same visible wrist break; they differ only in which muscle effort is missing ('the right hand providing the driving vector' vs 'at least a little bit of forearm tension'), which a camera cannot show.
